category_title: High school student with AD/HD exhibiting inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity
minimal_context: Marios is sitting in a traditional biology classroom, tasked with completing a worksheet based on an explanatory presentation of Lamarck's theory.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Marios, please look at the explanatory presentation on the board and use it to fill out your worksheet on Lamarck's theory.

STUDENT: I am not very interested... but OK... it is a relatively nice course.

TUTOR: Try to answer the first question on the worksheet based on the presentation.

STUDENT: I believe that biology is a course that a part of it should be carried out in the laboratory. No matter how good is the teacher’s intention and no matter how well he is informed a student cannot accept all these theories without seeing them happen.

TUTOR: We need to finish this worksheet right now. Keep trying to write down the answers.

STUDENT: (Daydreaming and looking toward the hallway) I missed the points necessary to complete the activity. I can't focus my attention on the details, it demands too much mental effort.

options.A: Use Evernote to take notes, organize work, and archive past biology worksheets.
options.B: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the biology worksheet and answering the presentation questions.
options.C: Probe the student to consider multiple plausible answers; deliberately step back from being the single knowledge source.
options.D: Implement a variety of teaching methods throughout the biology lessons and worksheet activities.
